description:
The narrowing at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:177, driven through the WHEN OTHER arm of the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at lines 99 to 102 - the last of the three arms, after WHEN DFHENTER at 94 and WHEN DFHPF3 at 96. EVALUATE is ordered: the first matching WHEN wins and the default is written last, so each arm is pinned by a case of its own rather than by one case that merely reaches a shared repaint (G30). Seventeen of the twenty cases in this directory drive DFHENTER, case10 pins DFHPF3, case01 stops at the EIBCALEN = 0 guard of line 82 before the EVALUATE is reachable at all, and this is the only case on WHEN OTHER.

WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80) at line 38 and ERRMSGO is PIC X(78) at app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY:260, and a COBOL alphanumeric MOVE fills the receiver from the LEFT and discards the overflow - so the surviving text is the LEADING seventy-eight characters and the trailing two bytes are lost. Line 101 moves CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY, which app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21 declares PIC X(50) carrying forty characters of text, into that eighty-byte field: WS-MESSAGE comes to hold forty characters and forty spaces, and the screen field forty characters and thirty-eight. The result is pinned twice, inside the send and again on the SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channel, so the width is part of the expectation rather than an incidental property of a string. case11 pins the guard rejection at eighty on WS_MESSAGE_80, and the two channels together are what make the DIRECTION of the truncation observable, because a receiver filled from the right would hold the trailing seventy-eight and shift every character two places. The invalid-key text is the right subject for that: of the four eighty-byte images COADM01C can produce one is the blank line 79 initialises, and a blank image reads identically from either end.

Twenty items are pinned, which is the count of name-labelled DFHMDF fields in app/bms/COADM01.bms, and every width is taken from the matching xxxI PICTURE clause of the symbolic map - the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items are length, flag and attribute metadata and are not payload, which is why ERRMSGC appears only as an attribute. Seven of the twenty cannot be observed from the service at all: the six header fields POPULATE-HEADER-INFO renders at lines 202 to 221 come from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at line 204, and ERRMSGO is the product of line 177 itself. Both belong to the controller if the service is to stay deterministic, which is why this case is driven through AdminMenuController as a plain Java object - constructed and its handler method called directly, with no MockMvc, no servlet container, no application context and no JobLauncher anywhere in the path (G51) - where case11 drives the service and pins thirteen.

The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant COADM01C's own version footer at line 267 carries, so it is anchored in the source rather than chosen and one clock governs every case in this directory. CURDATEO and CURTIMEO below are that instant rendered through the WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY and WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS groups of app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy:30-41, and US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default.

The echoed option is the field on this path most easily got wrong. WHEN OTHER does not perform PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, so lines 117 to 125 never run: the backward scan, the JUST RIGHT move into WS-OPTION-X at line 45, the INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' and the move into WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) at line 46 all belong to the DFHENTER arm. WS-OPTION is therefore never formed, the three-term guard at lines 127 to 129 is never evaluated, and CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME is never subscripted. OPTIONO is '7 ' and not '07' for precisely that reason - it is what the client re-supplied, handed back at the field's declared two characters and never normalised. No numeric parse happens anywhere on this path and no exception is any part of this expectation: a translation that parsed the field before deciding which arm it was on would throw where the program simply repaints, and this case must fail if it does. Each of those three guard terms is pinned elsewhere - case05 for WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC with OPTIONI '1x', case06 for WS-OPTION > CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT with '05' against the count of 4 that app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy:20 fixes, and case11 for WS-OPTION = ZEROS with a blank field. Worth recording beside them: app/bms/COADM01.bms:145-149 declares OPTION with ATTRB=(FSET,IC,NORM,NUM,UNPROT) and JUSTIFY=(RIGHT,ZERO), so a real 3270 would right-justify and zero-fill the keystrokes and refuse a non-digit outright, and the program validates the value itself anyway on the arm that reads it. That validation is preserved rather than dropped as redundant.

ERRMSGC below is the map's own default and not something the program wrote. app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157 declares ERRMSG with COLOR=RED and the WHEN OTHER arm moves no colour at all; the single colour COADM01C ever moves is the DFHGREEN of line 148, on the coming-soon path this case does not reach. Nor is there an asterisk to expect. Gate G38 is usually phrased around the DFHRED-plus-asterisk highlight CSSETATY applies, and COADM01C does not copy CSSETATY - its COPY list at lines 50 to 61 is COCOM01Y, COADM02Y, COADM01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - so DFHRED appears nowhere in its 268 lines. Expecting an explicit colour move or a highlight would be inventing behaviour; for this program G38 resolves to exercising both the ENTER and the REENTER path and expecting the map default red.

This is the REENTER half of that pair. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as 1, so line 87's IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false and line 89's MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO does not run: the REENTER path performs no output reset. OPTN005O to OPTN012O are the unpainted image below all the same, and for a different reason - BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at lines 228 to 263 iterates only to CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT, so lines 5 to 12 are never written at all, and a stateless projection holds no previous COADM1AO to preserve. That is what makes 'not reset' and 'never written' indistinguishable in the observable output, and saying so is more honest than asserting an echo the unit cannot produce: it reads OPTIONI and the AID from the received map and nothing else. The area is handed back unmutated with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT still 1, only the transfer path at line 141 zeroing it, and all sixteen COCOM01Y fields are pinned because statelessness is asserted by comparing the area in both directions (G37). The transaction ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CA00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) of lines 107 to 110, so no successor is named: nextProgram is absent, and the mapset and map are the screen this program repaints.

One derivation caveat is recorded here rather than glossed over. WHEN OTHER is an open arm - it catches every attention identifier that is neither DFHENTER nor DFHPF3 - so no single case can enumerate it, and the DFHPF5 below is a representative rather than a key the program names. It was chosen because common/CicsAid.java reproduces it as X'F5' from IBM CICS documentation, DFHAID being absent from this repository so that the byte cannot be read from source here at all (risk R-D), and because it is a key a terminal genuinely sends. The expectation is representative-independent by construction: the arm moves the same PIC X(50) literal and repaints the same screen whichever byte selected it, and nothing below is derived from the value X'F5'. Exhaustiveness over the arm is proved once, over every mnemonic CicsAid defines, in this program's gate class rather than twenty times over in the fixtures - including for the keys PfKeyResolver would resolve to a real token, because COADM01C does not copy CSSTRPFY and branching on a resolved token would make some other key behave like PF3 in a program that has no such behaviour.

Every expected value above is statically derived: read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms. Not one of them was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy program. None was, and none could be: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime here, the available COBOL compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository altogether. Only the provenance of the expected values changes - the twenty cases, the field-for-field comparison and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand unchanged - and because provenance is itself a stated success criterion, the deviation is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than quietly absorbed: risk R-A, as ParityCase's and ParityHarness's class documentation state it.
